concepts.title: Oceans and Continents: The Blue Planet
concepts.section: The Distribution of Water and Land
concepts.definition: Seen from space the Earth looks blue because almost three-fourths of its surface is water; the largest water bodies are oceans and the largest continuous land areas are continents.
concepts.key_idea: The blue planet divides into great waters and great lands, and both shape climate, life and history.
concepts.textbook_ref: fees102.txt, The Distribution of Water and Land

concepts.title: Water and Land in the Two Hemispheres
concepts.definition: Oceans and continents are not spread equally: maps drawn from above the North and South Poles show that most land gathers in the Northern Hemisphere while water dominates the Southern Hemisphere.
concepts.key_idea: Looking from each pole gives two different pictures of the same planet.

concepts.title: The Seven Continents of the Earth
concepts.definition: The Earth's land is grouped into seven continents: Asia, the largest, then Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia; islands such as ours sit near or within them.
concepts.key_idea: Continents are the great land containers of the world, each with its own size, climate and life.

concepts.title: The Five Oceans of the Earth
concepts.definition: The world's waters form five oceans, the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Arctic and Southern, joined into one great body that stirs climate and carries ships between continents.
concepts.key_idea: All oceans are one connected water body, divided by human naming into five.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why does the Earth appear mostly blue from outer space?

solution_template.explain: Water covers almost three-fourths of the surface of the planet.
Sunlight on that vast water makes the whole planet glow blue to astronauts.

worked_examples.question_pattern: How does a sea differ from an ocean?

solution_template.explain: An ocean is one of the five great bodies; a sea, bay or gulf is its smaller extension.
Waters nearer the land, like a bay or a gulf, are named seas in everyday use.
